# **Blur**

Source: https://github.com/junwen-k/tailwindcss-neumorphism-ui/blob/main/apps/storybook/src/stories/docs/blur.mdx

<Meta title="API/Blur" />

# **Blur**

> Utilities for controlling the blur of the neumorphism shadow.

| Class            | Properties                  |
| ---------------- | --------------------------- |
| `nm-blur-{blur}` | `--nm-shadow-blur: {blur};` |

This utility references the Tailwind CSS `--blur-*` theme variables. For a complete list of values, check the full documentation [here](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/blur).

## Basic Usage

### Controlling blur

To give an element a specific neumorphism shadow blur, use the `nm-blur` utility classes.

```html
<div class="nm-blur-xs ...">...</div>
<div class="nm-blur-sm ...">...</div>
<div class="nm-blur-md ...">...</div>
<div class="nm-blur-lg ...">...</div>
<div class="nm-blur-xl ...">...</div>
<div class="nm-blur-2xl ...">...</div>
```

## Applying conditionally

### Hover, focus, and other states

Tailwind lets you conditionally apply utility classes in different states using variant modifiers. For example, use `hover:nm-blur-md` to only apply the `nm-blur-md` utility on hover.

```html
<div class="hover:nm-blur-md ...">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

### Breakpoints and media queries

You can also use variant modifiers to target media queries like responsive breakpoints, dark mode, prefers-reduced-motion, and more. For example, use `md:nm-blur-lg` to apply the `nm-blur-lg` utility at only medium screen sizes and above.

```html
<div class="md:nm-blur-lg ...">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

## Using custom values

### Arbitrary values

If you need to use a one-off `nm-blur` value that doesn’t make sense to include in your theme, use square brackets to generate a property on the fly using any arbitrary value.

```html
<div class="nm-blur-[2px] ...">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

---

# **Color**

Source: https://github.com/junwen-k/tailwindcss-neumorphism-ui/blob/main/apps/storybook/src/stories/docs/color.mdx

<Meta title="API/Color" />

# **Color**

> Utilities for adjusting the neumorphism highlight / shadow color.

| Class                           | Properties                                |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `nm-{highlight/shadow}-{color}` | `--nm-{highlight/shadow}-color: {color};` |

This utility references the Tailwind CSS `--color-*` theme variables. For a complete list of values, check the full documentation [here](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/colors).

## Basic Usage

### Controlling color

To give an element a specific neumorphism highlight / shadow color, use the `nm-highlight` and `nm-shadow` utility classes.

```html
<div class="nm-highlight-cyan-500/50 ...">...</div>
<div class="nm-shadow-blue-500/50 ...">...</div>
<div class="nm-shadow-indigo-500/50 ...">...</div>
```

## Applying conditionally

### Hover, focus, and other states

Tailwind lets you conditionally apply utility classes in different states using variant modifiers. For example, use `hover:nm-shadow-white` to only apply the `nm-shadow-white` utility on hover.

```html
<div class="hover:nm-shadow-white ...">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

### Breakpoints and media queries

You can also use variant modifiers to target media queries like responsive breakpoints, dark mode, prefers-reduced-motion, and more. For example, use `md:nm-highlight-cyan-500/50` to apply the `nm-highlight-cyan-500/50` utility at only medium screen sizes and above.

```html
<div class="md:nm-highlight-cyan-500/50 ...">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

## Using custom values

### Arbitrary values

If you need to use a one-off `nm-highlight` or `nm-shadow` value that doesn’t make sense to include in your theme, use square brackets to generate a property on the fly using any arbitrary value.

```html
<div class="nm-shadow-[#50d71e] ...">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

# **Distance**

Source: https://github.com/junwen-k/tailwindcss-neumorphism-ui/blob/main/apps/storybook/src/stories/docs/distance.mdx

<Meta title="API/Distance" />

# **Distance**

> Utilities for adjusting the distance between the surface and the element.

| Class                   | Properties                         |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `nm-distance-{spacing}` | `--nm-shadow-distance: {spacing};` |

This utility uses the Tailwind CSS `--spacing` multiplier. For a complete list of values, check the full documentation [here](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/theme).

## Basic Usage

### Controlling distance

To give an element a specific neumorphism distance, use the `nm-distance` utility classes.

```html
<div class="nm-distance-1 ...">...</div>
<div class="nm-distance-2 ...">...</div>
<div class="nm-distance-4 ...">...</div>
<div class="nm-distance-5 ...">...</div>
<div class="nm-distance-6 ...">...</div>
```

## Applying conditionally

### Hover, focus, and other states

Tailwind lets you conditionally apply utility classes in different states using variant modifiers. For example, use `hover:nm-distance-2` to only apply the `nm-distance-2` utility on hover.

```html
<div class="hover:nm-distance-2 ...">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

### Breakpoints and media queries

You can also use variant modifiers to target media queries like responsive breakpoints, dark mode, prefers-reduced-motion, and more. For example, use `md:nm-distance-4` to apply the `nm-distance-4` utility at only medium screen sizes and above.

```html
<div class="md:nm-distance-4 ...">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

## Using custom values

### Arbitrary values

If you need to use a one-off `nm-distance` value that doesn’t make sense to include in your theme, use square brackets to generate a property on the fly using any arbitrary value.

```html
<div class="nm-distance-[2px] ...">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

# **Light Source**

Source: https://github.com/junwen-k/tailwindcss-neumorphism-ui/blob/main/apps/storybook/src/stories/docs/light-source.mdx

<Meta title="API/Light Source" />

# **Light Source**

> Utilities for controlling the light source for the neumorphism shadow.

| Class                | Properties                          |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `nm-light-source-t`  | `--nm-shadow-light-source: 0deg;`   |
| `nm-light-source-tr` | `--nm-shadow-light-source: 45deg;`  |
| `nm-light-source-r`  | `--nm-shadow-light-source: 90deg;`  |
| `nm-light-source-br` | `--nm-shadow-light-source: 135deg;` |
| `nm-light-source-b`  | `--nm-shadow-light-source: 180deg;` |
| `nm-light-source-bl` | `--nm-shadow-light-source: 225deg;` |
| `nm-light-source-l`  | `--nm-shadow-light-source: 270deg;` |
| `nm-light-source-tl` | `--nm-shadow-light-source: 315deg;` |

## Basic Usage

### Controlling light source

To give an element a specific neumorphism light source, use the `nm-light-source` utility classes.

```html
<div class="nm-light-source-tr ...">...</div>
<div class="nm-light-source-bl ...">...</div>
```

### Applying light source globally

Often, it's desirable for all elements to share the same light source direction for consistency. The `nm-light-source` utility classes can be placed high in the DOM tree so that all child elements inherit the same light source direction.

For example, in a Next.js app using the App Router, you can set the light source direction globally in the `app/layout.tsx` file:

```tsx
export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en" className="nm-light-source-tr">
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  )
}
```

## Applying conditionally

### Hover, focus, and other states

Tailwind lets you conditionally apply utility classes in different states using variant modifiers. For example, use `hover:nm-light-source-br` to only apply the `nm-light-source-br` utility on hover.

```html
<div class="hover:nm-light-source-br ...">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

### Breakpoints and media queries

You can also use variant modifiers to target media queries like responsive breakpoints, dark mode, prefers-reduced-motion, and more. For example, use `md:nm-light-source-r` to apply the `nm-light-source-r` utility at only medium screen sizes and above.

```html
<div class="md:nm-light-source-r ...">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

## Using custom values

### Arbitrary values

If you need to use a one-off `nm-light-source` value that doesn’t make sense to include in your theme, use square brackets to generate a property on the fly using any arbitrary value.

```html
<div class="nm-light-source-[17deg] ...">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

# **Protrude / Dent**

Source: https://github.com/junwen-k/tailwindcss-neumorphism-ui/blob/main/apps/storybook/src/stories/docs/shadow.mdx

<Meta title="API/Shadow" />

# **Protrude / Dent**

> Utilities for generating the neumorphism shadow.

| Class                    | Properties                                                                       |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `nm-{protrude/dent}-sm`  | @apply `nm-distance-1` `nm-shadow-black/15` `nm-highlight-white/50` `nm-blur-xs` |
| `nm-{protrude/dent}`     | @apply `nm-distance-2` `nm-shadow-black/15` `nm-highlight-white/75` `nm-blur-md` |
| `nm-{protrude/dent}-md`  | @apply `nm-distance-4` `nm-shadow-black/15` `nm-highlight-white/75` `nm-blur-lg` |
| `nm-{protrude/dent}-lg`  | @apply `nm-distance-4` `nm-shadow-black/20` `nm-highlight-white/75` `nm-blur-lg` |
| `nm-{protrude/dent}-xl`  | @apply `nm-distance-5` `nm-shadow-black/25` `nm-highlight-white/75` `nm-blur-lg` |
| `nm-{protrude/dent}-2xl` | @apply `nm-distance-6` `nm-shadow-black/35` `nm-highlight-white` `nm-blur-xl`    |

## Basic Usage

### Generating neumorphism shadow

To generate a neumorphism shadow, use the `nm-protrude` or `nm-dent` utility classes.

```html
<div class="nm-protrude ...">...</div>
<div class="nm-dent ...">...</div>
```

### Using the spacing variant

When composing from scratch, start with `nm-protrude` or `nm-dent` as the base and override individual properties with modifier utilities:

```html
<div class="nm-protrude nm-distance-4 nm-blur-sm nm-shadow-gray-500 nm-highlight-white">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

## Applying conditionally

### Hover, focus, and other states

Tailwind lets you conditionally apply utility classes in different states using variant modifiers. For example, use `hover:nm-protrude` to only apply the `nm-protrude` utility on hover.

```html
<div class="hover:nm-protrude ...">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```

### Breakpoints and media queries

You can also use variant modifiers to target media queries like responsive breakpoints, dark mode, prefers-reduced-motion, and more. For example, use `md:nm-protrude` to apply the `nm-protrude` utility at only medium screen sizes and above.

```html
<div class="md:nm-protrude ...">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>
```
